newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols bid, dlr/yen shrinks in US.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols bid, dlr/yen shrinks in US.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options in the one-month area edged up as spot briefly poked at 1.74 marks in the U.S., traders said.
On the other hand, a firmer dollar continued to erode volatilities for shorter-dated dollar/yen options, which had shot up earlier in the week.

"We're coming up to the higher end of the range (in spot dollar/mark)," said a U.S. bank trader in New York. He noted that the market's focus was shifting to the dollar's upside risk again, particularly in dollar/mark, as dollar/yen's big slide earlier in the week appeared to have put in a bottom.
He added that next week's European Union summit in Amsterdam and the June 20-22 Group of Seven summit in Denver offered plenty of event risk to support volatilities.
Still, time-decay concerns ahead of the weekend prompted selling in the very short dates like Monday expiries as dealers trimmed theta exposure off their books.
"We haven't seen marks or yen sold off too much ahead of the weekend as we usually do on Fridays," said a Canadian bank trader in Toronto, referring to the curve beyond one-month.
One-month dollar/mark was a touch off its morning highs in afternoon U.S. at 9.3/9.6 percent, up 0.3 point on the day.
In dollar/yen, activity was dominated by deals stemming from a huge purchase of one-year American style put options, a New York interbank broker said.
"Everybody was caught up spreading out of it," he said of market makers' hedge trades. "I think the bulk of the trade was taking place in the three-month and the six-month."
He said the original deal was probably bigger than $1 billion and priced at about 10.55 percent, about par with the standard at-the-money European-style.
The dollar/yen volatility curve, which had gone into steep inversion earlier in the week, flattened in consolidation.

Traders said the dollar's recovery to the 115-yen level cooled off the heat in downside strikes. When spot plunged to a seven-month low of 110.62 yen on Wednesday, a run for downside gamma pushed front-end volatilities sharply higher and skewed pricing enormously in favor of low-delta yen calls.
"It (spot) went way down and came way back, and it hasn't dropped at all since then," said John Bird, senior currency options analyst at Technical Data.
He added that dealers now had a relatively even strike-price exposure at present spot levels, the site of range-trading for a few weeks prior to this week's slide.
One-month dollar/yen volatility stood at 11.4/11.7 percent. Three-months out to one-year were roughly flat at 10.4/10.6 percent.

Risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, continued to narrow their skew for yen calls. One-month 25-delta, which had favored yen calls by about 2.5 point on Wednesday, came in to about 1.4/1.7 today.
"They haven't really come off as much as I would have thought," Bird remarked, however. There still seemed to be demand to protect the downside, he said.
